addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

Here is the complete inventory of background workers, runners, and scheduling infrastructure in this codebase (Memos, a Go note-taking server).

## 1. Server Startup Flow

The server entry point is `/bench/home/work/cmd/memos/main.go`. The `rootCmd.Run` function creates a `server.Server` and calls `s.Start(ctx)`. That method (in `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`, line 101) starts the HTTP server in a goroutine (line 124) and then calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` (line 129).

Shutdown is handled by `s.Shutdown(ctx)` (line 134), which calls `stopBackgroundRunners()`, `closeLongLivedConnections()` (closes the SSE hub), `shutdownHTTPServer()`, and `waitBackgroundRunners()`.

---

## 2. Background Workers/Runners ACTIVELY Started by the Server

### 2A. S3 Presign Runner (ACTIVE -- started at server boot)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`
- **Type**: Interval-based background runner (ticker loop)
- **Interval**: Every 12 hours (`const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, line 27)
- **How started**: In `Server.startBackgroundRunners()` at `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`, lines 153-173:
  1. `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` is called synchronously (an immediate one-time pass at startup, line 163)
  2. Then `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` is launched in its own goroutine (line 167-170)
- **What it does**: Iterates over all S3-type attachments in batches of 100. For each attachment whose presigned URL is older than 4 days, it generates a new presigned URL (valid for 5 days) and updates the attachment record in the database.
- **Lifecycle**: Managed via a dedicated `context.WithCancel`. The cancel function is stored in `s.backgroundRunnerCancels`. On shutdown, all cancel functions are called, and `s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()` waits for completion.

### 2B. Webhook Async Dispatch Workers (ACTIVE -- started via `init()`)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`
- **Type**: Channel-based async queue with worker pool
- **How started**: The `init()` function (line 42) spawns **4 goroutines** that read from `asyncPostQueue` (a buffered channel of capacity 128).
- **What it does**: Workers dequeue `WebhookRequestPayload` messages and POST them to external webhook URLs via HTTP. Failed dispatches are logged but not retried.
- **Lifecycle**: These goroutines run for the lifetime of the process. The channel is never closed, so the workers run until process exit.
- **Triggered by**: `PostAsync()` (line 184) enqueues payloads. This is called from the memo service webhooks code at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`.

### 2C. Email Async Dispatch Workers (ACTIVE -- started via `init()`)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/internal/email/email.go`
- **Type**: Channel-based async queue with worker pool
- **How started**: The `init()` function (line 16) spawns **2 goroutines** that read from `asyncEmailQueue` (a buffered channel of capacity 128).
- **What it does**: Workers dequeue email requests and send them via SMTP. Failed sends are logged but not retried.
- **Lifecycle**: These goroutines run for the lifetime of the process. The channel is never closed.
- **Triggered by**: `SendAsync()` (line 55) enqueues email requests.

### 2D. Cache Cleanup Goroutines (ACTIVE -- started when Store is created)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go`
- **Type**: Interval-based cleanup loop (ticker)
- **How started**: `cache.New(config)` (line 76) spawns a background goroutine via `go c.cleanupLoop()` (line 83). Three cache instances are created in `store.New()` at `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` lines 51-53:
  1. `instanceSettingCache`
  2. `userCache`
  3. `userSettingCache`
- **Interval**: Every 5 minutes (`CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, configured at store.go line 43)
- **What it does**: Iterates over all cache entries and removes expired ones. Also calls `OnEviction` callbacks if configured (currently `nil`).
- **Lifecycle**: Each cache goroutine listens on `stopChan`. On `Store.Close()` (store.go line 72), all three caches are closed, which signals the goroutines to exit and waits for confirmation via `closedChan`.

### 2E. SSE Hub + Per-Connection Heartbeat (ACTIVE -- created at server construction)

- **File (Hub)**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`
- **File (Handler)**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`
- **Type**: Event broadcasting hub with per-connection heartbeat tickers
- **How started**: `NewSSEHub()` is created inside `apiv1.NewAPIV1Service()`, which is called during `NewServer()` at server.go line 76. The SSE hub itself is a passive data structure (no background goroutine). However, each SSE client connection gets a heartbeat ticker (every 30 seconds, line 64 of sse_handler.go) that runs for the lifetime of that connection.
- **What it does**: The hub manages SSE client subscriptions and broadcasts memo/reaction change events to connected clients. The heartbeat keeps connections alive.
- **Lifecycle**: On shutdown, `s.closeLongLivedConnections()` calls `s.sseHub.Close()` which closes all client channels, causing all per-connection handler goroutines to exit.

### 2F. PAT Last-Used Timestamp Update (ACTIVE -- fire-and-forget goroutines)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go`
- **Type**: Fire-and-forget goroutine per PAT authentication
- **How started**: `recordPATUsage()` at line 179 spawns a `go func()` that updates the personal access token's last-used timestamp in the database.
- **What it does**: Updates the `last_used` timestamp for a Personal Access Token after successful authentication.
- **Lifecycle**: Each goroutine is short-lived and independent. No tracking or cancellation.

---

## 3. Scheduling Infrastructure That EXISTS but is NOT Used by the Server

### 3A. Cron Scheduler Package (EXISTS -- NOT wired into server startup)

- **Directory**: `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/`
- **Files**:
  - `doc.go` -- Package documentation
  - `scheduler.go` -- Core `Scheduler` struct with `Register()`, `Start()`, `Stop()` methods
  - `job.go` -- `Job` struct with `Name`, `Schedule` (cron expression), `Handler`, `Timezone`, `Tags`
  - `parser.go` -- Full cron expression parser supporting 5-field and 6-field formats (wildcards, ranges, lists, steps)
  - `middleware.go` -- Middleware pattern: `Recovery()`, `Logging()`, `Timeout()`, `Chain()`
- **What it provides**: A full-featured, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler with timezone support, middleware wrapping, and graceful shutdown.
- **NOT USED**: There are **zero non-test imports** of `"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"` anywhere in the codebase. It is only referenced in test and example files:
  - `internal/scheduler/example_test.go`
  - `internal/scheduler/scheduler_test.go`
  - `internal/scheduler/job_test.go`
  - `internal/scheduler/middleware_test.go`
  - `internal/scheduler/parser_test.go`
  - `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`
- **Conclusion**: This is a fully implemented but completely unused piece of infrastructure. The server instead uses a simpler ad-hoc ticker pattern for the S3 presign runner and `init()` goroutine pools for webhooks/email.

### 3B. Memo Payload Runner (EXISTS -- `Runner.RunOnce()` NOT called at server startup; only `RebuildMemoPayload` used inline)

- **File**: `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`
- **Type**: Batch-processing runner (no ticker/cron -- only a `RunOnce` method)
- **What it provides**: `Runner.RunOnce()` iterates over ALL memos in batches of 100 and rebuilds their payload (tag extraction, property computation from markdown).
- **NOT USED as a runner**: The `Runner` struct is never instantiated in the server startup path. There is no import of `"github.com/usememos/memos/server/runner/memopayload"` in `server.go`. The only imports of this package are in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, where only the standalone function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload()` is called inline during memo creation (line 108) and memo update (line 447) -- not the runner.
- **Conclusion**: The `Runner` struct and its `RunOnce()` method appear to be designed for one-time migration/rebuild operations but are not wired into the server's normal startup or background processing.

---

## Summary Table

| Component | Location | Type | Started By | Active? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S3 Presign Runner | `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` | Ticker (12h interval) | `Server.startBackgroundRunners()` | YES |
| Webhook Workers (x4) | `internal/webhook/webhook.go` | Channel queue + worker pool | `init()` | YES |
| Email Workers (x2) | `internal/email/email.go` | Channel queue + worker pool | `init()` | YES |
| Cache Cleanup (x3) | `store/cache/cache.go` | Ticker (5min interval) | `cache.New()` via `store.New()` | YES |
| SSE Hub + Heartbeats | `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`, `sse_handler.go` | Event hub + per-conn ticker (30s) | `NewAPIV1Service()` / per HTTP request | YES |
| PAT Usage Recording | `server/auth/authenticator.go` | Fire-and-forget goroutines | Per PAT auth request | YES |
| Cron Scheduler | `internal/scheduler/` | Full cron scheduler | **NEVER** | NO -- unused |
| Memo Payload Runner | `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | Batch runner (RunOnce only) | **NEVER** (only `RebuildMemoPayload` used inline) | NO -- Runner unused |
